evidence: src/presentation/api/WorkshopController.ts:29-31 openOrder: `if (input.estimatedHours <= 0 || input.estimatedHours > 40) { throw new FleetError('Estimates must be between 0 and 40 hours', 400); }`. This is a business limit on work-order estimates, written into a presentation controller.
The constructor injects MaintenanceService and MileageService from src/business/services (domain), which presentation may depend on. That is ordinary dependency wiring.
logHours, closeOrder and reading only delegate to the business services and format the result through workOrderJson (presentation), which fits the presentation role.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: WorkshopController is a presentation-layer controller. Most of it fits that role. It takes plain input DTOs that the project declares itself, injects business services that the presentation layer may depend on, and formats the results with a presentation helper. The exception is openOrder. Before it calls the service, it checks `input.estimatedHours <= 0 || input.estimatedHours > 40` and throws a FleetError with the message 'Estimates must be between 0 and 40 hours'. The 40-hour ceiling is a policy about work-order estimates. That is a domain invariant, not a check on input format or shape, so MaintenanceService.open or the WorkOrder model in the business layer should own it. Because the rule sits in the controller, any other caller of MaintenanceService.open can skip it. The candidate flags point to this same spot, and the source confirms them. The other methods (logHours, closeOrder, reading) only delegate to the services and format the result.

violations.message: openOrder enforces a domain rule: an estimate must be over 0 and at most 40 hours (`estimatedHours <= 0 || estimatedHours > 40`, which throws FleetError). This rule belongs in the business layer (MaintenanceService.open or the WorkOrder model), not in a presentation controller.
